content.title: About
content.content: Ice cream cone is a classic dessert consisting of a crunchy waffle cone filled with a scoop of chocolate ice cream. The chocolate flavor is achieved with cocoa mass and natural flavorings. This treat is popular worldwide as a light summer snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial ice‑cream cone appeared in the United States in the early 1900s.
Chocolate ice cream often contains a small amount of cream, making it richer than fruit‑based versions.
Waffle cones can be slightly sweet or lightly salty, which accentuates the chocolate taste.
In many countries the cone is served with extra toppings such as nuts, sprinkles, or berry sauce.
Ice‑cream cones are frequently used in “tallest cone” contests.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Chocolate ice cream made with dairy provides calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Milk ingredients supply a modest amount of vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Carbohydrates and a small amount of fat give a fast source of energy, useful as a light snack.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Cocoa mass contains flavonoids that may have antioxidant effects.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Chocolate ice cream typically contains a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy‑based products may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Nut and soy allergies
items.content: Some recipes include nuts or soy lecithin, posing a risk for allergic individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of cream and sugar, the cone is fairly calorie‑dense; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Hard waffle cone
items.content: The crunchy cone can be a choking hazard for very young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the ice cream cone immediately after scooping so the cone stays crisp. Optional toppings include sprinkles, chopped nuts, caramel sauce, or fresh berries. Avoid letting the ice cream sit too long, as the cone will become soggy.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The finished cone is best enjoyed right away. If you need to store, keep the ice cream in a freezer at –18 °C and the cone in a dry place to prevent moisture absorption. Before serving, let the ice cream soften slightly to avoid soaking the cone.
